items.title: Accor Builds Caution Into Outlook Over France Unrest and Middle East
items.summary: Accor is guiding to a flat fourth quarter globally, partly out of caution after France's recent riots and uncertainty about wars in the Middle East.

items.title: NYC’s Horse-Drawn Carriages To End by 2028
items.summary: New York is ending one of its most iconic tourist attractions. Pedicabs have been floated as an alternative, but lawmakers say that industry has its own issues.

items.title: American Airlines Expects a 2026 Loss. How It Plans to Turn a Profit in 2027.
items.summary: American CEO Robert Isom said he was confident that American’s premium investments will pay off in 2027.

items.title: Wyndham Courts AI Booking Agents in Push for Direct Bookings
items.summary: The Super 8 and La Quinta franchiser is opening its inventory to Meta's Muse, OpenAI, and Instinct. Morgan Stanley analysts think AI agents could cost hotel groups less per booking than online travel agencies do.

items.title: IHG Says It’s Winning Hotels From Rival Brands
items.summary: IHG’s conversion machine is firing in the Americas, but its growth story ultimately depends on a pipeline to the east of Europe that had a difficult Q3.

items.title: Saudi Strikes Spill Over Into Gulf Tourism, Operators Say
items.summary: Houthi strikes are measurably cutting Saudi demand, but the UAE’s damage so far shows up in operator sentiment and forward bookings more than in the data. The winter season will test whether travelers view the Gulf as a single risk.

items.title: Oyo Parent Prism Halves IPO Size, Leaving More Debt to Be Repaid From Cash Flow
items.summary: A smaller IPO is being sold as a sign of strength, but Prism may simply be playing it safe. After two abandoned IPO attempts, a smaller raise could mean it doubts demand at its old valuation, or just wants a smoother sale.

items.title: IHCL Is Racing Past Its 2030 Goal of 700 Hotels. Now It Needs a Bigger Number
items.summary: Hitting its 2030 target years ahead of schedule is a clear sign that India’s branded hotel market is moving faster than expected. The bigger question now is whether quality can keep pace when a brand like Ginger doubles its footprint so quickly.
